prompt: A detailed cutaway centers on a credit-card-sized green circuit board—the system-on-module—its surface densely packed with a visible processor, memory modules, graphics chip, and storage, shown halfway inserted into a socket on a larger surrounding circuit board that bears partially completed traces for custom sensors, motors, and antennas. Behind this assembly, the composition splits into two mirrored worlds: on the left, stacks of identical modules sit in benign industrial lighting beside a warehouse robot, emphasizing mass production and low cost, while on the right, the exact same module is being installed into the cramped electronics bay of a silhouetted cruise missile or drone, so that a single visual glance conveys how the standardized, ready-to-use computing core travels effortlessly from civilian automation to military hardware.
